config.title: Toggle Visibility

intro.title: Toggle Visibility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that shows and hides content with a button click. You will learn how to use Vue's reactive data system to track whether content is visible. The main concepts you'll practice are conditional rendering with v-if and handling click events with v-on. By the end, you'll understand how to control UI visibility dynamically using Vue's reactivity.
intro.usecase: Toggling visibility is a core pattern in interactive web applications. You'll use it to show or hide form sections based on user input, expand and collapse detailed panels in dashboards, and manage dropdown menus or modal dialogs. Mastering this concept allows you to build dynamic, user-friendly interfaces that respond instantly to user actions.

objectives: Initialize a reactive boolean state to control visibility
Construct a click handler that toggles the boolean state
Apply conditional rendering to display or hide content based on state
Bind a button's click event to the toggle handler
Manipulate the DOM to dynamically update the UI in response to state changes
Integrate a visibility toggle into a functional Vue component

steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template's div, below the heading, with the text 'Toggle Visibility' and wire it to the toggle handler using the @click directive.

<button>{{ isActive ? 'Deactivate' : 'Activate' }}</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button text will dynamically change between 'Show' and 'Hide' based on the isVisible state.
successCriteria: Button text uses a ternary expression with isVisible to display 'Hide' when true and 'Show' when false.
